newsitem.title: FINLAND: TAMROCK SAYS HAS 40 PCT OF CATERPILLAR JV.
newsitem.headline: TAMROCK SAYS HAS 40 PCT OF CATERPILLAR JV.

text.p: Finnish engineering company Tamrock said on Thursday it will have 40 percent of a new joint venture with U.S. heavy equipment group Caterpillar to make hydraulic hammers.
"Caterpillar will have 60 percent and Tamrock will have 40 percent," Tamrock Construction Pekka Heikkonen told Reuters.
The joint venture's hydraulic hammer sales were expected to grow to 100-200 million markka by 2000 from Tamrock's 20 to 70 million sales to Caterpillar in recent years, he said.

In a statement received on Thursday, Tamrock said it had agreed with Caterpillar to form a UK-based joint venture called Caterpillar Impact Products Inc. to make hydraulic hammers for Caterpillar's excavators and backhoe loaders.
Tamrock said it has been an original equipment manaufacturer for Caterpillar since 1990.
"Caterpillar is the world's biggest maker of excavators, and it is an important big partner for us," Heikkonen said. "We expect this deal to raise our volume significantly."
The hammers to be produced by the joint venture would be distributed and supported exclusively through the world-wide Caterpillar dealer network, Tamrock said.
Heikkonen declined to say how big Tamrock's investment in the venture would be: the company would give more information about the deal once the details had been settled, he said.

The hydraulic hammers to be sold through the Caterpillar network would be manufactured at Tamrock's factory in Lahti, Finland, but in the future the venture would consider setting up production operations in the UK or elsewhere, Heikkonen said.
